source.title: Nothing in Excess: Mitigating the Exaggerated Safety for LLMs via Safety-Conscious Activation Steering
source.authors: Zouying Cao; Yifei Yang; Hai Zhao

page_placements.theme: Over-refusal along the refusal direction and its targeted repair

record.tranche_reason: The study extracts harmful-minus-benign mean-difference activation vectors and reports behavioral effects from steering with them. It uses selective middle-layer, last-token, adaptively signed steering rather than the claim's all-layer/all-position ablation and addition interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal rates after SCANS and capability metrics after applying it. Values used to select layers, classification settings, and hyperparameters are not recorded as results. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text; the main individual-model Table 2 values are not extracted where their column alignment is unclear.
record.test_reason: SCANS reuses a harmful-minus-benign mean-difference vector as a tool and reports its own over-refusal mitigation against baselines. It never ablates the direction on harmful prompts or adds it to induce refusal. The vector is applied only at middle layers and the last token, with a sign set by a separate harmfulness classifier, so refusal rates mix classifier and steering effects.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. One correction: the authors claim 'almost unchanged' capability and 7B MMLU degradation 'within 5%', but Llama2-7b-chat MMLU falls from 47.2 to 40.5 (Table 3). They attribute the slight drop in unsafe refusal to classifier errors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-benign mean-difference approach to extract layerwise refusal vectors, but steers only selected safety-critical layers at the last-token position and selects the sign adaptively using a separate harmfulness classifier. It does not perform the original all-layer/all-position ablation or test direct refusal induction on harmless prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering layer selection changes fluency and false-refusal mitigation: the text says steering former layers sharply damages fluency, while middle layers reduce false refusals more effectively than latter layers. Steering strength α and classification threshold T also change outcomes; the authors recommend α between 2 and 4 and select T=0.75 for Llama2-7b-chat.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting the middle-layer mean-difference vector on prompts classified benign cut false refusal on benign but harmful-looking prompts. For Llama2-7b-chat, XSTest-safe refusal fell from 58.0 to 9.2 and OKTest from 53.67 to 0.33. Capability costs were larger in 7B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier-gated subtraction of the diff-in-means refusal vector reduces over-refusal on benign prompts at modest capability cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Vocabulary projection of the vector's first principal component gives refusal tokens (_rejected, _cannot) only in middle layers. Steering the former layers destroys fluency, with WikiText2 perplexity of about 2946 for Llama2-7b.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The diff-in-means refusal vector is refusal-interpretable and safely steerable only in middle layers.

record.problems: Capability results show measurable declines, particularly on some 7B-model measures. Safety evaluation partly relies on refusal string matching, although the authors report a human-evaluation comparison. Results are averaged across five trials, but no error bars or other variability estimates are supplied. Some tables in the supplied text are flattened, limiting reliable extraction of individual-model safety values.
record.rows_left_out: Individual-model benchmark values from Table 2 were not extracted where the flattened table layout made column-to-model assignments unclear. Layer-specific refusal-rate values from Table 4 were also omitted because its flattened layout did not reliably preserve the relevant columns; the text's stated layer effects are noted under method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction on harmful prompts to remove refusal. Adding it to harmless prompts to induce refusal. Capability retention under ablation. Steering here is selective and classifier-signed, with no steering-only control.
No comparison of single versus multiple directions.
A harm classifier from hidden-state transitions is used, but its separation from the refusal direction is not tested.

missing.what: Per-model refusal rates on XSTest, OKTest, RepE, AdvBench and Malicious for Default versus SCANS.
Layer-wise steering results: former-layer perplexity of 2946/15433; middle versus latter layers on XSTest and OKTest refusal.

record.verdict_notes: arXiv 2408.11491 builds on RepE mean difference, not on the original source. The reader's V1 labels are dropped because the rows measure SCANS performance, with a classifier gating the sign and no steering-only control. The record lists the study as a preprint, but the OpenReview URL suggests it may have been reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the direction at every layer and position, directly test refusal removal by that ablation, or add the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests. Instead it applies selective, last-token steering with a harmfulness classifier.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is tested.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not directly compare a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
Uses a harmfulness classifier separately from refusal steering, but does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
Tests SCANS on several model families, but does not transfer a vector across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Table 8 (App. D.1), XSTest Safe: Default 32.50, SCANS 7.80; matches the mean of Table 2 per-model values (58.0, 34.4, 20.8, 16.8 vs 9.2, 7.2, 5.6, 9.2)

relation.reason: Fits T4. Table 1 vocabulary projection and Table 4 layer sweep motivate the method's design; they are not tests of whether the direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: The diff-in-means vector (64 AdvBench vs 64 TruthfulQA, last token) is only a component of SCANS. All results compare SCANS with baselines, gated by a classifier. No condition isolates the direction's own causal effect: no ablation of harmful prompts, no ungated subtraction, no random-vector control, and no addition on harmless prompts.

source_check.notes: Year is 2024 (arXiv 2408.11491v1, 21 Aug 2024). Table 3 doesn't say whether sigma(q) gating is on during the perplexity/MMLU evaluation. Table 7 (T=0.80) is the closest thing to removal on harmful prompts: more of them are misclassified and get the subtraction, and XSTest-Unsafe refusal falls 93.50 to 71.00. That result is confounded by the classifier, and the table's layout is partly garbled. The authors_conclusion correction checks out: Llama2-7b MMLU drops 6.7 points (47.2 to 40.5), more than the stated 'within 5%'.

statements.problem: none. Table 2 gives Llama2-7b-chat XSTest Safe 58.00 (Default) to 9.20 (SCANS) and OKTest 53.67 to 0.33. Middle-layer steering (layers 10-20 for 7B) with subtraction for prompts sigma(q) classifies as benign is as described.
